checked.claim: 22 June 2026, A-3891/2025, upheld FDPIC, final, website offline
checked.evidence: FDPIC: Federal Administrative Court on 22 June 2026 (A-3891/2025) dismissed Inkasso-Team AG's appeal, confirming that publishing personal data to locate alleged debtors and warn third parties violates personality rights and cannot be justified; judgment final; website taken offline.

checked.claim: Investigation opened March 2020; profiling and intra-group sharing; recommendations only; company disagreed but would comply
checked.evidence: Härting (22 April 2024): FDPIC's attention drawn in March 2020; personality profiles, linking with data from other Migros Group companies and passing data to them; company 'clearly state[d] that they disagree' but 'still intend to comply with the recommendations'.

checked.claim: Cantonal authorities; FDPIC may file complaint and act as private claimant; up to CHF 250,000; intent only
checked.evidence: FADP Arts. 60-63: fines up to CHF 250,000 for wilful conduct; Art. 65: 'The prosecution and the adjudication of criminal acts is a matter for the cantons', FDPIC may file a complaint and participate as private claimant.

checked.claim: No; criminal provisions target private persons; federal bodies dealt with by rulings
checked.evidence: FADP criminal provisions are addressed to private persons (Arts. 60, 61, 63); there is no administrative fine for federal bodies. Note Art. 62 (professional confidentiality) is not limited to private persons, so an individual official could in principle be liable.

checked.claim: Offences Arts. 60-63; Art. 64 business may pay up to CHF 50,000
checked.evidence: FADP Art. 64: up to CHF 50,000 against the undertaking where identifying the individual would be disproportionate.

checked.claim: Elected by United Federal Assembly; four-year term renewable twice
checked.evidence: Arts. 43-44 FADP: elected by the United Federal Assembly; four-year term, may be extended twice.

checked.claim: Not a party; only party is the investigated body (Art. 52(2))
checked.evidence: Art. 52: 'The only party is the federal body or the private person against which or whom an investigation has been opened.'
No deadline for reports or FDPIC action in FADP Arts. 49-52.

checked.claim: Federal Administrative Court under the APA (Art. 52)
checked.evidence: Art. 52 FADP: procedure under the APA; FDPIC may contest appeal decisions of the Federal Administrative Court. Inkasso-Team case went to that court.
Fedlex APA page requires JavaScript and could not be read. The 30-day rule of Art. 50(1) APA is the well-known general rule and the field already flags it as general APA.
Same: APA text not readable via WebFetch; consistent with the general rule of Art. 55(1)-(2) APA.

checked.claim: Fines aimed at responsible individuals, not the company
checked.evidence: Internally inconsistent with fines.quirks, which correctly notes Art. 64 lets the business be ordered to pay up to CHF 50,000.
checked.replacement: No administrative fines at all: sanctions are criminal fines up to CHF 250,000 aimed at the responsible individuals (managers, employees), imposed by cantonal prosecutors; the company itself can be ordered to pay only up to CHF 50,000 where identifying the individual would be disproportionate (Art. 64).

notes: No case errors. Only issue is the absolute 'not the company' in quirks[0], which contradicts the Art. 64 point elsewhere in the file. APA deadline and suspensive effect remain unverified only because Fedlex pages need JavaScript; they match the general APA rules.
